title: Admission
description: The only packet permitted to move a claim's status. Every other packet proposes; this one disposes. It exists so admission is a recorded, replayable operation rather than an unrecorded judgement — the six acceptance conditions in SKILL.md need somewhere to be written down as having actually been checked, and NOT_RUN needs to be sayable. VERIFIED lives here and nowhere else, which is what makes its absence from frame-result-v1 mean something.

base_revision.description: The state revision this admission applies against. Applying it to any other revision is rejected, not merged.

result_ref.description: Required whenever a STATUS MOVES, and only then. An admission that changes the SHAPE of the problem — Explorer adding sub-claims, setting a dependency mode — rests on no evidence and referencing a result it does not have would be a fiction. Demanding it unconditionally meant a decomposition could only enter the state as a side effect of somebody producing an artifact, which is Explorer's own output made unrecordable. Nothing is weakened: the delta schema already forces every added claim to OPEN with no evidence, so a structural admission cannot smuggle a conclusion.

receipt_ref.description: The verification receipt this admission rests on, bound by seal rather than named. Required for any accepted status: without it `checks` is a set of assertions by whoever wrote the admission, and the enforcement chain ends in a self-report at exactly the point it matters. With it, the reducer DERIVES each check from the receipt and refuses any disagreement with what was asserted.

decided_by_role.description: Which role decided this admission. Only Explorer arbitrates: a production role admitting its own output is the failure the no-merge invariant exists to prevent, and until this field existed that invariant was a sentence in a document rather than something the state machine could refuse. The schema admits any role because the schema describes SHAPE; the reducer refuses anything but explorer because that is POLICY. Encoding the policy as a const would make the refusal a formatting complaint instead of the reason it exists.

granted_status.description: The status this admission grants. Required in spirit when decision is ACCEPT. This is the only place VERIFIED may appear in any packet.

checks.description: What the admitting role BELIEVED about each acceptance condition. It is a record, not the decision: the reducer derives every condition from the supplied receipt, result, reviews, and its own closure computation, and refuses any disagreement between the two. Nothing here is required, because forcing a role to state a verdict on a condition it has no evidence about produces guesses — and a guess that happens to match is indistinguishable from knowledge. State what you checked; the reducer states what is true.

review_refs.description: The frame-review-v1 packets discharging independent_review. A review whose independent flag is false does not count toward it.

evidence_refs.description: Every entry echoes the target and result hashes it was gathered under, so evidence harvested from a neighbouring claim is detectable without dereferencing it.

delta.description: The state transition, typed rather than free text, so an admission can be replayed instead of retold. A newly added claim is forced OPEN with no evidence — a pre-established claim cannot be injected through a delta.

ceiling.description: The strongest status this claim may ever reach, set once when the claim is created and never afterwards — there is no delta operation that raises a ceiling. It comes from the resolved pack: the strongest `max_status` among its tiers, lowered further if the pack is provisional. This is how a provisional pack's cap stops being a printed warning and starts being something the reducer refuses to exceed.

evidence_sha256.description: May be EMPTY for a claim whose content is exactly the conjunction or disjunction of its dependencies. Such a claim has no artifact of its own and needs none: its evidence is the receipts its dependencies were admitted on, each of which passed its own pack's gates. Requiring at least one item meant a decomposition could be built, worked and closed at every leaf, and the parent that motivated it could never be admitted — every decomposition dead-ended at the node it existed for. The reducer still refuses an empty list unless the claim really is a dependency node whose closure holds, and it caps the granted status at the weakest admitted dependency.

set_dependencies.description: Dependency edits record the mode transition, not just the new edges — silently turning an AND node into an OR node would make an incomplete claim look closed.

supersede.description:
Claims cancelled because a sibling won the race they were in. §5.1 has described this since it was written and there was no operation to record it, so a race could be PLANNED and its outcome could not be written down — the loser stayed runnable and every later plan offered it again.

It moves no status, on purpose. Losing a race teaches nothing about a claim, and the frame's rule is that process states never appear as epistemic ones. The annotation is what makes revival free: clear it and the claim is back in the wave with no transition needed, which is what has to happen when the winner later fails.

payload_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of this packet with payload_sha256 removed: sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes.

actor.description: Who executed this packet, as the orchestrator sees it. The frame cannot verify identity — sessions, workers and processes belong to the orchestrator — so it records what was attested and refuses to treat an unattested separation as a demonstrated one. Two packets sharing an actor_id are the same actor whatever their role labels say.

actor_id.description: Opaque, orchestrator-assigned. Stable within a run.

attested_by.description: `orchestrator` means something outside the run vouched that this actor is distinct. `self`, or an absent actor block, means nobody did — independence is then NOT_RUN, which puts CONDITIONAL and VERIFIED out of reach.

attestation_ref.description: Optional orchestrator-side handle for the attestation.

allOf.description: A status that needs evidence needs a result to point at.
